en: The Scripture on Auspicious and Inauspicious Times and Days and the Good and Evil Constellations and Planets Spoken by Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva and Various Sages, Volume One.
By the Kai-fu Yitong Sisi, Teci, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial, Duke of Su.

The Imperial Preceptor of Daguangzhi at Daxingshan Monastery, the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Amoghavajra—who was granted a fief of three thousand households, invested with the purple robe, posthumously honored as Minister of Works, and bestowed the title of Great Supervisor—translated this under imperial decree. His disciple Yang Jingfeng, a scholar of the grassy wilds in the capital, composed these annotations during the second year of the Qianyuan era, while the Master was translating this text.
Sima Shi Yao of Duanzhou took charge of collecting [the materials],
yet was unable to arrange them in proper order,
resulting in a text whose meaning is cluttered and redundant.
Fearing that students might find it difficult to apply,
the disciple Yang Jingfeng, a scholar from the wilds,
personally received the instructions of the Upādhyāya.
I have further revised and annotated it,
completing the editorial work so that it may be transcribed and practiced.
Let each of my disciples hold a copy.
At that time, the year was the *xuāoxiāo* (the first lunar mansion), the second year of the Guangde era of the Great Tang. Part One:

The Introductory Section, Chapter on Determining the Constellations and Planetary Alignments, from the *Xiuyao Li Jing*. Regarding the introductory section, Chapter One: Determining the Constellations and Planetary Alignments—When heaven and earth were first established.
The essence of cold and heat transforms into the sun and moon;
the crow and the hare contend in their opposition, generating and sustaining the myriad things.
They divide the lunar mansions and establish the palaces, overseeing and marking the various categories of existence.
The sun governs the position of Yang;
it proceeds in accordance with the constellations, taking thirteen lunar mansions:
Zhang, Yi, Zhen, Jiao, Kang, Di, Fang, Xin, Wei, Ji, Dou, Niu, and Nü.
Reaching up to the midpoint of the lunar mansion Xū (虛),
which coincides with the center of the hour of Zi (子),
it is divided into six palaces.
Although the Son of Heaven, the Sun, and the Son of Heaven, the Moon,
both have the five planets as their ministers and assistants, the radiance of the sun is fierce and intense;
this is because things of similar nature resonate with one another.
The Yang-creature lion serves as the guardian deity of the palace;
its moonlight is cool and refreshing,
for things of like nature resonate with one another.
The signs of Cancer and Capricorn are the presiding deities of the houses.
Furthermore, the nature of the Sun is firm and righteous,
while the nature of the Moon is gentle and benevolent.
The principles [of governance] are used to sustain the subordinates and bestow kindness upon ministers;
likewise, the sun and moon each receive their divine palaces with equal allotment,
while the five planets vary according to their swiftness or slowness of arrival.
These are the planets Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, and Saturn;
they are arranged in this order,
whereby their movements and the varying speeds of their traversals are thereby made manifest.
The twelve palaces (*dvādaśa-rāśi*) are the stations through which the seven luminaries pass;
each sequentially reveals fortune and calamity, as well as the patterns of disasters and auspiciousness.
Furthermore, each palace possesses its own deity and form.
This serves to manifest the symbolism of the palaces.
Furthermore, each palace corresponds to a tube and the arrayed lunar mansions;
with nine legs, all classes of beings are mutually influenced.
The moon is fifty yojanas in width;
it governs life, death, and the auspiciousness or inauspiciousness of the capital.
Its primary function belongs to the sun and the moon.

The Sun is fifty-one *yojanas* wide and consists of the essence of wind; Venus is ten *yojanas* wide and consists of the essence of space; Jupiter is nine *yojanas* wide and consists of the essence of the moon; the lunar mansions (*nakṣatras*) are eight *yojanas* wide and consist of the essence of fire; Mars is seven *yojanas* wide and consists of the essence of the sun; Saturn is six *yojanas* wide. The smallest of the stellar bodies is one *krośa* wide. The lower surface of the solar palace is made of crystal (*sphaṭika*), having the nature of the essence of fire.
The warmth of the sun can illuminate all things;
the lapis lazuli beneath the moon palace is cool and can illuminate the myriad phenomena.
The sun, moon, and various celestial bodies,
placed in space by the karma of sentient beings,
remain suspended by riding upon the wind.
When it is at the midpoint of Mount Sumeru, above the Yugaṃdhara mountains,
it revolves through the twenty-seven lunar mansions and the twelve zodiacal signs (*rāśi*).
I shall now fully explain the divisions of these signs and mansions.
It is merely a matter of the diagrams and texts.
The first star has four legs;
the constellation Chang (Tent) has four legs.
One leg is the position of the Great Sun;
its deity is like a lion.
Therefore, it is named the House of the Teacher (Libra).
It presides over the conferral of office and the acquisition of wealth.
If a person is born under this house, [these matters will be fulfilled].
By the nature of the law, one shall possess sufficient spirit, wealth, honor, and filial piety;
it is fitting that one hold the command of military affairs.
The second wing has three feet.
The constellation Zhèn has four legs;
the constellation Jiǎo has two legs;
and the position of the planet Chénxīng is therein.
Its deity is like a woman;
therefore, it is named the "Woman's Palace" (Nv-gong).
It presides over matters concerning wives, concubines, and women.
If a person is born under this mansion, it is according to the Dharma that they will find it difficult to obtain a heart-felt position;
yet, possessing many children and abundant wealth, they shall hold a high office and thus be fit for the duties of a palace chamberlain.
The third lunar mansion, Jie (角), has two feet;
Kang (亢) has four feet;
Di (氐) has three feet.
The position of Venus is here;
its deity is like a scale,
hence it is named the Palace of the Scale.
It presides over the affairs of the treasury.
If a person's birth falls under this house,
it is according to the Dharma that they will be upright in heart, impartial and just, faithful and respectful, and possess great wealth.
The position of the Treasury is assigned to the joined palms.
Fourth is the one-footed Ascendant,
and the fourth is the four-footed Ascendant.
The mind has four feet;
it occupies the position of Mars (Hénghuò).
Its spirit is like a scorpion.
Therefore, it is called the House of Scorpio.
It presides over many illnesses and matters concerning the subjugation and division of the body.
If a person is born under this house:
By the nature of the Dharma, one will suffer from many illnesses, have a meager appearance, harbor an evil mind, and be envious and jealous.
One will be fit for the role of a patient with palms joined.
This is the fifth tail and fourth leg.
The Winnowing Basket has four legs;
the Dipper has one leg.
The planet Jupiter occupies this position.
Its deity is like a bow;
therefore, it is named Bow-Palace (Cāpakuṇḍa).
It presides over matters of joy, celebration, and the acquisition of wealth.
If a person is born under this mansion,
it is according to the Dharma that they will possess abundant strategic planning and mental ingenuity,
and they shall attain the rank of a high minister or general.
The sixth lunar station, Dou (Dipper), has three legs;
Nü (Woman) has four legs;
and Xū (Void) has two legs.
The planet Venus (Tianxing) is situated therein;
its deity is like Makara,
and thus it is named the Makara Palace.
One presides over matters of strife and contention.
If a person’s birth falls under this mansion, by the nature of the law, their mind will be coarse;
they will commit the five heinous crimes and show no respect for their wife or children.
The duty of inflicting capital punishment is assigned to the palms joined together.
The six positions listed above, in total, belong to the division of the Great Sun (Sūrya).
The six positions below belong, in total, to the division of the Great Moon (Candra).
The seventh [storey] has two legs;
the eighth has four legs;
the ninth has three legs.
The planet Saturn is situated therein.
Its deity is like a vase;
therefore, it is named the Vase Mansion (Kumbha).
It presides over matters of sovereignty, victory, and strength.
If a person’s birth falls under this house,
it is according to the law that they will naturally be fond of practicing loyalty and integrity, possess sufficient learning, and be wealthy and abundant.
The office of the Gasshō School consists of one leg for the eighth chamber and four legs for the wall.
Gui has four legs;
it is the position of the planet Jupiter (Sui-xing).
Its deity is like a fish.
Therefore it is named the Fish Palace (Mīnabhavana).
It governs matters concerning the appointment and reception of official rank.
If a person's birth falls under this palace, [they will experience such affairs].
He is destined for the ranks of generals and ministers without fail or loss;
he possesses learning, wealth, honor, and integrity, and is suited for the office of a high-ranking official.
His palms are joined in the mark of a ministerial position.
The ninth lunar mansion, Lou (Pleiades), has four legs;
Wei (Hyades) has four legs;
Mao (Taurus) has one leg.
The planet Mars occupies this position;
its deity is like a sheep,
hence it is named the Sheep Palace.
The ruler possesses deeds of exemplary conduct.
If a person's birth falls under this mansion,
it is according to the Dharma that they shall possess great merit and long life.
Furthermore, he was able to practice patience;
with palms joined, he took charge of the kitchen.
The tenth mansion, Mṛgaśiras, has three feet.
Bi has four legs;
Zi has two legs;
this is the position of Taibai (Venus).
Its deity is like an ox;
therefore it is named Ox-Palace (Goṣṭha).
It presides over matters concerning four-footed livestock.
If a person is born under this mansion,
according to the Dharma, they shall possess sufficient merit and virtue, have many kinsmen and friends,
enjoy longevity, and be honored and respected by others.
He was appointed to the post of stable master.
The eleventh lunar mansion, Jyeṣṭhā, has two feet;
the third lunar mansion, Āśleṣā, has four feet.
The well has three legs;
the position of the planet Venus (Chenxing) is there.
Its deity is like a husband and wife.
Therefore, it is called the "Palace of Lust.
It presides over matters concerning conception, pregnancy, and descendants.
If a person's birth falls under this palace, [such are their characteristics].
It is fitting that he have many wives and concubines and receive the love and respect of others;
he is fit for the office of holding the keys to the gates.
The twelfth is the well with one leg.
The Gui (Ghost) has four feet;
the Liu (Willow) has four feet;
this is the position of the Great Yin.
Its deity resembles a crab;
therefore, it is named the Crab Mansion (Karkaṭa-rāśi).
It presides over matters of litigation and disputes within official government offices.
If a person is born under this mansion,
by the nature of things they will possess an evil disposition, be deceitful and clever, yet short-lived;
they are suited for positions involving the administration of justice, prisons, and litigation.
In the second month of spring, at the new moon of the ancient month of Bai-bocha,
when the celestial bodies were aligned with the lunar mansion Lou (Pūrvabhādrapadā),
the path was level, the shadow was upright, and the seasonal energy was harmonious at midday.
All things gradually flourish and everything increases.
Brahmā rejoices and ordains it as the beginning of the year. The Great Tang calls the "Auspicious Wind" (Jingfeng) the start of the year, reckoning from the month of Yin;
India takes the month of Mao as the head of the year.
Thus, while the months of the Great Tang are all designated as the first, second, third, fourth,
up to the twelfth,
in India they all rely on the fifteenth night of the bright fortnight (*śuklapakṣa*) to determine the lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) in which the moon resides.
For the sake of naming the months, the month when the moon is in the *jian-mao* position is called the "Crescent Moon" (*Jiǎo yuè*),
and the month when it is in the *jian-chen* position is called the "Root Moon" (*Dǐ yuè*);
thus, one simply refers to them as the months of the Crescent, the Root, the Heart, and the Winnowing Basket.
Nor does it concern the months of Mārgaśīrṣa (Mao), Caitra (Chen), or the first, second, and third lunar months.
This is a point of divergence between the Eastern and Western traditions;
students should first understand this. Now, these two points shall be explained in detail as follows.

The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Jiao corresponds to the second month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Mao. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Di corresponds to the third month of the Tang calendar;

it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Chen. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Xin corresponds to the fourth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Si. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Ji corresponds to the fifth month of the Tang calendar;

it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Wu. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Nü corresponds to the sixth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Wei. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of Shi corresponds to the seventh month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Dipper points toward the position of Shen.

The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Liu* (the Pleiades) corresponds to the eighth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *You*. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Mao* (the Orion's Head) corresponds to the ninth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *Shu*.

The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Zui* (the Orion's Foot) corresponds to the tenth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *Hai*. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Gui* (the Ghost Star) corresponds to the eleventh month of the Tang calendar;

it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *Zi*. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Xing* (the Star Star) corresponds to the twelfth month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *Chou*. The "Jingfeng" wind of the month of *Yi* (the Wing Star) corresponds to the first month of the Tang calendar; it is the period when the Big Dipper points to the position of *Yin*. The new explanations are as follows.
Jingfeng said, "When first translated from the Sanskrit original,
the terminology was obscure; thus,
those of the Tang dynasty were confused."
Not understanding its underlying cause,
one realizes that unless one has long practiced and achieved mastery, it will ultimately be difficult to succeed. Therefore,
I now request that you expound upon the ancient principles to bring them into a new application.

Having taken the months and days from the calendar and arranged them into a table of constants (*siddhānta*), he further produced a diagram of the twelve terrestrial branches (*dvādaśa-rāśi*) for the lunar months of the Great Tang,
correlating them with the names of the palaces and harmonizing them with the sequence of the lunar mansions (*nakṣatra*).
Thereafter, the principles will become clear and observable without concealment; may those of high talent in the present age understand this intent.

Day thirty. Regarding the constellations Wei, Bi, Lou, Mao, Zi, Jing, Liu, Zhang, Zhen, Kang, Fang, and Wei, the Immortal asked:
"In general, among the twenty-seven lunar mansions of the heavenly way, some are broad and some are narrow."
All are equally distinguished by their four feet;
the movements of the moon are sometimes ahead and sometimes behind,
as evidenced by the discrepancies between the celestial observations and the various explanations.
"How is the suitability of the lunar mansions (nakṣatras) for specific days determined?
The Bodhisattva replied,
"In general, there are three types of lunar mansions that accord with the Dharma."
First is prior conjunction, second is sequential conjunction, and third is simultaneous conjunction.
By knowing these three, the *nakṣatra* (lunar mansion) alignment can be known.
What is prior conjunction?
The six lunar mansions of Kui, Lou, Wei, Mao, Bi, and Zi constitute the "preceding conjunction.
What constitutes the "simultaneous conjunction"?
The twelve lunar mansions of Shen, Jing, Gui, Liu, Xing, Zhang, Yi, Zhen, Jiao, Kang, Di, and Fang constitute the "simultaneous conjunction."
What is meant by "conjunction" (*anvādhāna*)?

The nine lunar mansions of Heart (*hṛdaya*), Tail (*jyeṣṭhā*), Ladle (*mṛgaśiras*), Dipper (*ārdrā*), Maiden (*punarvasu*), Void (*puṣya*), Peril (*āśleṣā*), Chamber (*maghā*), and Wall (*pūrvaphalgunī*) constitute conjunction.
Generally, when a mansion is situated before the moon and the moon resides behind the mansion, it is called "prior conjunction."
The moon is in front of the lunar mansion, and the mansion is behind the moon;
it is like a calf following its mother that they are said to be "in conjunction.
When the mansion and the moon move side by side, they are said to be "in parallel conjunction. Jingfeng stated: "This is the general principle of celestial phenomena."
The west is the front and the east is the back.
For example, if the moon is to the east of a lunar mansion (*nakṣatra*) and the mansion is to the west of the moon, then the mansion is in front of the moon and the moon is behind the mansion.
All other cases should be understood by analogy with this.
The verse says:
Six lunar mansions have not yet arrived; the preceding ones are called "conjunction. Twelve mansions are conjoined with the moon on its left or right;
nine mansions follow it like a calf follows its mother. One should know that when the constellation Kṛttikā is on duty, this is the case.

2. Chapter on the Births Corresponding to the Daily Constellations and Planetary Positions (Nakṣatra-yoga-jāta-prakaraṇa), Second in the *Sūrya-siddhānta-tantra*. Diagram of the Kṛttikā [constellation].
Kṛttikā consists of six stars; its shape is like a razor.
He is the Fire God.
His clan name is Mupinipeigu.
He consumes milk and curd.
On this day governed by the lunar mansion,
it is appropriate to perform fire rituals, boiling and decocting,
and to calculate the number of livestock.
Mixing medicinal ghee;
constructing cowsheds and sheep pens;
planting trees within the residence.
Engaging in military expeditions against rebels or suppressing the violent is auspicious;
shaving the head is likewise auspicious.
However, if used for tailoring clothes, one will certainly be burned by fire.
For those born under this lunar mansion,
it is dharma that they should be mindful of goodness, have many sons and daughters,
be diligent in study, and possess dignified deportment.
By nature parsimonious and harsh, yet possessing eloquence in speech; the "Scenic Wind" says that among the celestial phenomena of the Central Kingdom,
the Pleiades (Mao) consist of seven stars and preside over the armies of the Hu.
It is a lunar mansion of the Western Region.
However, upon examining the scriptural texts now,
it appears that the descriptions of the stars mostly do not accord with those of China.
Readers may hastily give rise to doubts; I now request that you consult Chinese astronomy.
I have illustrated the stars beneath their feet in two diagrams.
Those who read this with discernment will find their minds free from any confusion.
Bhittu. The shape of the five lunar mansions of Bhittu is like a half-cart.
Bhaṣa-bhaṭṭi is the deity.
His surname was Gautama;
he ate deer meat on this day of the lunar calendar.
One should engage in agriculture and sericulture, plant crops,
repair fields and dwellings,
and clear and regulate the drainage channels.
Building bridges and roads are deeds that bring long-term peace and stability;
one should not engage in lending money at interest.
Furthermore, those born under this lunar mansion will spend their wealth on grain and rice;
if they use it to tailor clothing, they will inevitably have many affairs to attend to.
This applies to people born when this mansion is in the ascendant.
In accordance with the Dharma, they possess abundant property and sufficient sons and daughters;
by nature they are intelligent and fond of practicing charity;
they have a discerning mind and are sparing in speech.
The mind does not waver.

His gait is like that of a bull-king, possessing dignified bearing. Jingfeng says: "Zhongguo (the Central Kingdom) has the constellation Bi consisting of eight stars; it presides over border troops and is the lunar mansion of the West."
Diagram of Jīva.
The three stars of Jīva are shaped like the head of a deer.
It is the deity of the moon.
His clan name was Brahmadatta;
he ate deer meat.
This was the day of his birth-star.
One should construct houses,
as well as manufacture banners, streamers, beds, canopies,
and furniture; enter new residences, perform marriages, bathe, and prepare one's attire.
Entering the altar to worship the stellar deities brings good fortune and eliminates calamities. On this day,
if one cuts clothing, it will be bitten by mice.
This person was born under this lunar mansion;
according to the Dharma, they are destined for renown and exemplary conduct,
possessing a handsome appearance and a mind that is cautious and pure.
One who loves taking medicine will surely gain its efficacy;
their heart and mouth remain hidden and secret, and their movements are neither frivolous nor agitated.
Such a person is fond of the Dharma and employs affectionate courtesy; among the Chinese constellations, they correspond to the three stars of Jue (Beak).
The General of the Army is the lunar mansion of the West.
This is the diagram of the Three Stars (San Tu).
The constellation Ārdrā is shaped like a dot on the forehead;
its presiding deity is Rudra,
whose family name is Lauhitya.
It feeds on blood.
On this lunar day,
it is appropriate to seek wealth and to dig the earth.
Selling milk products, boiling ghee, pressing oil,
and performing various harsh or violent tasks; furthermore,
if one uses [this day] to cut clothing, one must be extremely careful of the calamity of rats.
Those born under this lunar mansion are, according to the Dharma, naturally fierce, stubborn, and prone to anger;

they possess venomous speech and a hard heart, remaining undaunted when facing critical affairs. Jingfeng says that among the celestial phenomena of the Middle Kingdom, the constellation Shen consists of ten stars and presides over generals.
It is a lunar mansion of the Western Quarter.
Its diagram depicts a well;
the two stars are shaped like the rafters of a house.
He is the Sun Deity.
His clan name is Vasiṣṭha.
He eats ghee cakes.
On this day presided over by the lunar mansion,
it is appropriate to bestow gifts upon the poor; one will certainly obtain great fruit,
and whatever actions are undertaken will surely achieve success.
Furthermore, it is auspicious for sacrificing to Heaven, for marriage, and for receiving wealth;
however, it is inauspicious for compounding medicines or taking them as tonics.
If one uses this day to cut clothing, there will surely be separation.
For those born under this asterism,
it is according to the Dharma that wealth may either be present or absent;
they possess affection, fame, and reputation, and serve as officials who benefit others.
Even if there is misfortune related to officialdom, one will attain liberation.
One's nature is prone to illness, yet one will have many sons and daughters.
Because of one's high status, there may be sudden difficulties or calamities.

Regarding the "Exemplary Conduct" (*jingxing*), it is somewhat similar to the "Pure and Upright. Regarding the "Auspicious Wind" (*jingfeng*): in the Chinese celestial system, the Well (*jing*) asterism consists of eight stars and presides over the Celestial Gate (*tiānmén*).
It is a lunar mansion of the South.
[The *Guǐtú* states:]...
The three stars of the ghost constellation are shaped like a vase.
They are the deities Ālikaṣāṭi;
their clan name is Mauñjāyana.
On this day presided over by the lunar mansion, one should consume honey, molasses, sugar, rice-flower, and milk porridge;
it is auspicious for performing all manner of activities and for praising long life.
It is auspicious for the study of Secret Mantra when attending to royal affairs, various matters of adornment,
being invested with office, ascending to a position, entering a ritual mandala,
or receiving a protective talisman.
If one uses [this material] to tailor clothing, there will certainly be auspicious and superior matters.
As for those born under this lunar mansion,
according to the Dharma, their physical features are naturally upright and handsome, free from deformity, and they possess mental power and strength.
One who possesses these [constellations] will have many learned followers, wives and concubines, and abundant wealth and treasures;

they will be capable of overseeing and managing affairs and will be surrounded by sufficient kin and associates. Feng said: "The Zhongguo (Central State), Tianwen (Heavenly Patterns), and Gui (Ghost) five stars preside over the official bureaucracy; they are the lunar mansions of the South."
The Willow Diagram (*liù tú*).
The Willow consists of six stars and is shaped like a snake;
it is a deity.
The clan name is Mandaraya;
they eat the flesh of pythons.
This is the day of the lunar mansion’s alignment.
It is appropriate to act with fierce determination to suppress rebels,
